hook.en: A boy tries to snatch a woman's purse late at night. Instead of handing him to the police, she takes him home. Langston Hughes turns a crime into a lesson in trust.

objectives.en: Retell the story in your own words
Analyse the characters of Mrs Luella Bates Washington Jones and Roger
Discuss the themes of trust, dignity and second chances

narration.en: A boy tries to snatch a woman's purse late at night. Instead of handing him to the police, she takes him home. Langston Hughes turns a crime into a lesson in trust.

body.en: Late one night, a teenage boy, Roger, tries to snatch the large purse of a big, strong woman, Mrs Luella Bates Washington Jones. The purse is heavy, he loses his balance and she catches him at once. Instead of calling the police, she drags him to her small room, makes him wash his face, and asks why he did it: he wanted a pair of blue suede shoes. She tells him she too once did things she is not proud of. She shares a simple meal with him, leaves her purse within his reach to show trust, and finally gives him ten dollars for the shoes, asking him to behave. Roger, overwhelmed, can barely say "Thank you, ma'am" before she shuts the door; he never sees her again. Read the prescribed text itself; this guide is in our own words and quotes nothing.

points.en: Roger tries to snatch a purse and fails
Mrs Jones takes him home instead of to the police
Washing, a meal, trust, and a gift of money

text.en: character contrast
Physically strong, fearless, firm
Kind, understanding, has a past of her own
Teaches through trust, not punishment
Young, poor, neglected (no one at home to feed him)
Wants shoes, not crime for its own sake
Changes: from running away to wanting to be trusted
His thanks is all he can say, and it is not enough
A small phrase for a large gift of kindness

text.en: Exposition
Late night; a woman walks home alone
with a large purse on her shoulder.
Rising action
Roger tries to snatch it, falls,
and is caught and held firmly.
Climax
In her room she leaves the door open and
her purse near him; he chooses to stay.
Falling action
They eat together; she speaks of her own
past; she gives him money for shoes.
Resolution
At the door he can only manage
a few words of thanks; they never meet again.

body.en: Trust and kindness change people more than punishment: Mrs Jones treats Roger with dignity and expects good behaviour, and he responds by wanting to earn her trust. Poverty and neglect explain, but do not excuse, his act. The story also shows that people who have made mistakes can still guide others; Mrs Jones admits her own past. Hughes tells the story mostly through simple dialogue and action, with humour in Mrs Jones's bluntness and a quiet, open ending.

steps.en: Roger grabs the strap of the purse
The purse is too heavy and he falls
Mrs Jones kicks him and holds him by the collar
She takes him home and makes him wash his face
He learns she will not hand him to the police
She gives him ten dollars for blue suede shoes

explanation.en: The story moves from the failed theft, through the surprising hospitality, to the gift.

problem.en: Why does Mrs Jones help Roger instead of punishing him?

steps.en: She sees that he is poor and uncared for, with no one at home to feed him.
She remembers her own youth and the things she did that she is not proud of.
She believes trust can teach him more than the police could.
She wants him to get the shoes honestly next time, without stealing.

answer.en: She understands his situation, sees herself in him, and believes kindness and trust will change him.
